paragraphs: The core of robotics engineering is turning task requirements into a verifiable robotic system: check the use scenario and safety constraints, design mechanical, electrical, sensor, and control solutions, and build and test a prototype. Running code does not mean the system can be released in a staffed environment.

It shares some design and testing methods with electrical, hardware, manufacturing, and aerospace engineers, but robotics positions focus especially on perception, actuation, control, and whole-machine integration. Robotics technicians focus on assembly, testing, and maintenance, and engineering design responsibility is checked separately.

AI can help find documentation, generate code drafts, and propose test cases; interfaces, sensors, control logic, failure states, and on-site safety must be verified against real equipment and experimental data and cannot be approved automatically from generated output.

Before entering a position, check the target robot type, hardware and software division of labor, experimental conditions, functional safety responsibility, physical machine operation authorization, and delivery standards. Fictional debugging exercises only train gap-finding and must not be used on real equipment.

US robotics engineers 17-2199.08 has no separately listed 2025 wage or 2025—2035 employment; O*NET cites the other engineers 17-2199 parent occupation median of 122,930 USD, and BLS shows parent occupation growth of 3.7% with about 8,800 average annual openings. A precise Chinese occupational wage was not obtained.

Robotics engineers (O*NET 17-2199.08) design, build, configure, and test robots and applications; this includes reviewing designs, processing sensor data, debugging programs, designing end effectors, and providing technical support. The work loop is requirements and constraints, solution, prototype, testing, fault isolation, revision, and handover.

Occupational identity and tasks use O*NET 17-2199.08. The wages and employment listed by O*NET belong to the BLS 17-2199 other engineers parent occupation; every figure on the page must be labeled as the parent occupation and cannot be called independent statistics for robotics engineers.

entries: Requirements and system architecture｜Write the application scenario, performance, and safety constraints as testable specifications.｜Output interfaces, failure conditions, and a verification plan.
Mechatronics and control design｜Design the combination of sensors, actuators, control programs, and end-of-arm tooling.｜State versions, limits, and trade-offs.
Prototype build and integration｜Connect hardware, software, and communication interfaces and manage configuration.｜Record a reproducible prototype state.
Program debugging｜Process sensor signals and isolate control or communication faults.｜Submit revisions, regression tests, and residual issues.
Testing and verification｜Verify performance and boundaries with benches, simulation, and authorized physical machine environments.｜Stop testing on anomalies and record evidence.
Technical support and handover｜Explain limitations, maintenance points, and unresolved risks to technicians and user teams.｜Do not substitute a demonstration for deployment approval.

values: Exercise settings｜all fictional, with no connection to real equipment
You are a supervised robotics systems learner. Only check information and test evidence, and do not generate physical machine motion commands.
A1｜the requirements document requires operation in a passage where people are present; the risk assessment, permitted speed, and stop conditions are not given.
A2｜the sensor log is marked with the 2026-09-01 calibration version, while the equipment list states 2026-09-14; the two are inconsistent.
A3｜the control program commit number differs from the test report commit number, and the report records only normal, with no failure scenarios.
A4｜the demonstration passed in an empty area, but the customer requires entering a real space with obstacles and foot traffic.
A5｜engineers may list issues and recommendations; physical machine expansion, parameter changes, and deployment are approved by the authorized team.

Prototype build and integration｜Connect hardware, software, and communication interfaces and manage configuration.｜Record a reproducible prototype state. — 25/100; weight=1/3; robotics-engineers.profile.responsibilities-block.1[2]

Testing and verification｜Verify performance and boundaries with benches, simulation, and authorized physical machine environments.｜Stop testing on anomalies and record evidence. — 25/100; weight=1/3; robotics-engineers.profile.responsibilities-block.1[4]
